source_batch.unit_label: BRBL C U02 MSMED Act: Choose the Facilitation Council route and distinguish conciliation from arbitration

facts.statement: Any party may refer the amount-due dispute under section 18. Conciliation precedes arbitration after failed terminated conciliation. Supplier-location jurisdiction can cover buyer anywhere in India; references have stated 90-day decision period. State establishes councils of 3-5 members chaired by specified industry official.

payload.title: A reference starts a process; it is not an instant award
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 18 allows a party to refer the specified amount-due dispute to the Facilitation Council. The Council conducts or refers conciliation. If that conciliation fails and is terminated without settlement, the statutory route proceeds to arbitration conducted by the Council or a referred institution or centre. Do not label a failed negotiation an award.

The supplier-location jurisdiction provision can reach a buyer anywhere in India. The Act states ninety days from making a reference for its decision; this is not evidence that an actual file was decided in time. The State establishes Councils; their statutory membership range is three to five and the designated industry official chairs them. Later procedural amendments and case law remain review issues.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an out-of-state buyer alone defeat the supplier-location jurisdiction provision?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The provision expressly addresses a buyer located anywhere in India.

payload.stem_md: An eligible supplier is within a Council jurisdiction and its buyer is in another Indian State. The buyer argues that interstate location alone defeats the section 18 jurisdiction. What does the statutory text indicate?

options.text_md: The buyer can always choose a foreign forum by email
options.explanation_md: No such unilateral forum power follows from this provision.

options.text_md: The stated supplier-location provision can cover a buyer anywhere in India
options.explanation_md: Interstate buyer location alone does not negate the express statutory reach.

options.text_md: Only disputes between neighbours in one town qualify
options.explanation_md: The text does not impose this same-town restriction.

options.text_md: The National Board must first approve the reference
options.explanation_md: The Board policy role is not the Council reference process.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Interstate buyer location alone does not negate the express statutory reach.

payload.stem_md: Conciliation under the stipulated section 18 process fails and is formally terminated without settlement. Which next step fits the statutory sequence?

options.text_md: The failed meeting automatically becomes a paid decree
options.explanation_md: Failed conciliation is not itself an award or satisfaction of debt.

options.text_md: The supplier loses the debt because settlement failed
options.explanation_md: Failure to settle does not extinguish the underlying claim.

options.text_md: Only a fresh National Board policy meeting can continue the file
options.explanation_md: The dispute process is assigned to the Council/arbitration route.

options.text_md: The Council takes up arbitration or refers it to the stated institution or centre
options.explanation_md: The text provides arbitration after unsuccessful terminated conciliation.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The text provides arbitration after unsuccessful terminated conciliation.
